precepts.text: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings. That is the true washing: cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, not speech. Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; if ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land, but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Naaman was told, “Wash, and be clean”, and when he believed and obeyed the word of the prophet, he was clean. Isaiah shows what the true washing is: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; Learn to do well”.

Put away the evil of your doings: that's the true washing. Cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, action, action. Not speak well, do well. “seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

“though your sins be as scarlet”, bloodshot red, “they shall be as white as snow”, if you learn to do well. “though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.” But it hangs on obedience: “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword”.

That is Naaman. At first he refused and went away in a rage. When he humbled himself and did according to the saying of the man of God, his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. His belief and his obedience are what made him clean.

precepts.text: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Naaman believed that the word of the prophet would heal him if he followed the commandment, going down to the river Jordan and dipping seven times. That belief is what healed him of his leprosy.

David prays the same way: “Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.” Truth in the inward parts is what the Most High desires. Then: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

The water of the Jordan did not do it by itself; the Jordan was muddy water, and Naaman would rather have had the rivers of Damascus. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins. Naaman obeyed the word, and he was made clean, his flesh like the flesh of a little child.

precepts.text: John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins: the same river Naaman was cleansed in.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
We read about Naaman going down into the river Jordan to be cleansed. Luke brings us back to that same river: John “came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins; As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

The baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins, preached about Jordan. Naaman was washed of his leprosy in the Jordan, and John preached the washing away of sins in the same Jordan. Nothing is accidental with the Most High.

It was Christ who healed Naaman, working through Elisha by his spirit. And John in the Jordan was preparing the way of that same Lord.

precepts.text: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. The same Jordan, the number and the river pointing to the same Christ.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.” Christ went unto John the Baptist to be baptized, and in what river? Jordan: the same river that Naaman had to dip in seven times.

Seven represents completion. Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan, completion in the river Jordan, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. The number and the river both point to the same Christ.

Who did the healing for Naaman? Not Elisha on his own. Elisha was working by the spirit of Christ; Christ is the one who did the healing, and he used Elisha as the prophet. So when Christ himself comes to the Jordan, it is the same one who cleansed Naaman there, the one who makes us clean.

precepts.text: Many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian. Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history. “I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.”

Then the point: “And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.” Of all the lepers, the one cleansed was the one who humbled himself, believed, and went down and dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God.

And seven also represents complete deliverance. Naaman dipped seven times and was delivered from his leprosy; Christ, the one whose spirit healed him through Elisha, spoke of it himself.

precepts.text: Naaman, captain of the host of Syria, was a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.
precepts.point: Nebuchadnezzar came to praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, for those that walk in pride he is able to abase. The heathen understand that the Most High is greater than all other gods; it is our people that want a god that does not look like them.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Naaman is another non-Israelite who came to know what Jethro knew. He was “captain of the host of the king of Syria”, “a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.”

A great man of another nation, honourable and mighty in valour, and yet a leper. That is who the Lord was about to heal, and who would confess, like Jethro, that the Lord is greater than all gods.

precepts.text: Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan and was clean, and confessed there is no God in all the earth but in Israel; a heathen vowed to sacrifice to no other god but the Lord.
precepts.point: Nebuchadnezzar came to praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, for those that walk in pride he is able to abase. The heathen understand that the Most High is greater than all other gods; it is our people that want a god that does not look like them.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Naaman “went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.” Then he came back and stood before the man of God and said, “Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel”. Those are Jethro’s words: now I know. A Syrian, healed of his leprosy in Jordan, confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel.

His faith was so strong he asked for “two mules’ burden of earth”, “for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the Lord.” A heathen vowed to sacrifice to no other god but the Lord.

He even asked pardon for bowing in the house of Rimmon with his master: “when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the Lord pardon thy servant in this thing.” He knew that bowing there, only because his master leaned on his hand, was a thing to ask pardon for. That is how far a non-Israelite went once he knew the Lord is greater than all gods.

precepts.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
precepts.point: Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

precepts.why:
“To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:” everything has its time, receiving included.

Gehazi went in and stood before his master, and when Elisha asked, “Whence comest thou, Gehazi?” he answered, “Thy servant went no whither.” Elisha said, “Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?” It was not the season for it.

Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, “The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever.” He went out from Elisha’s presence “a leper as white as snow.”

precepts.text: There is a time to get, and a time to lose, which is what Elisha explained to Gehazi, that there was a time to receive the gifts and this was not it.
precepts.point: Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

precepts.why:
“A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;” That is what Elisha explained to Gehazi: there was a time to receive the gifts, and this was not it.

Gehazi was hasty to grasp. He lied to his master, but Elisha’s heart went with him, and for taking out of season the leprosy of Naaman cleaved to him and to his seed for ever.

This shows how Israel thought then, and how the nation still thinks now: hasty to grasp things by unjust means instead of waiting for the time to get.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Naaman, captain of the host of Syria, was a great man but a leper. A captive Israelite maid pointed him to the prophet in Samaria, and he came with silver, gold and raiment, because a man will give everything for his health.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: 'Went not mine heart with thee?' The spirit of the Lord reveals; Bishop once asked a brother twice whether he was dealing drugs, and the next class played the raid on his grow house. When the prophets ask about business you told nobody, take heed.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Elisha sent word to wash seven times in Jordan. Naaman was wroth because he expected the prophet to come out and wave his hand; he had better rivers at home. That pride almost cost him his healing. When the Lord says do, do; stop wanting God to do it your way.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: His servants talked sense into him, he dipped seven times, and his flesh came again like a little child's. He offered a blessing and Elisha refused it, as the Lord liveth, and sent him away in peace with his treasure.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Gehazi, Elisha's servant, saw all that glitter and ran after Naaman with a lie: my master sent me, two sons of the prophets have come, give them a talent of silver and two garments. Covetousness made him lie, and when Elisha asked where he had been, he lied again. Sin was added to sin because he never controlled the covetousness.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: The leprosy of Naaman shall cleave unto thee and thy seed for ever, and Gehazi went out a leper white as snow. God does not like covetous people; Gehazi was judged immediately. Many of us are not judged right away and think we are good, but the money we love will destroy us.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, is a great man with his master and honorable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria. He is a mighty man of valor, but he is a leper.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: The Syrians had gone out by companies and brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid, and she waits on Naaman's wife. This maid is an Israelite sister serving in a foreign house.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: She tells her mistress that if only her lord were with the prophet in Samaria, he would recover him of his leprosy. Naaman goes and tells his lord what the maid of Israel said.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: The king of Syria sends Naaman with a letter to the king of Israel, and Naaman takes ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment. The letter asks the king of Israel to recover Naaman of his leprosy.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: When the king of Israel reads the letter, he rends his clothes and asks, am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to recover a man of his leprosy. He thinks the king of Syria is seeking a quarrel against him, knowing he has no such power.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: When Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has rent his clothes, he sends to the king asking why, and says let the man come to him, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Naaman comes with his horses and chariot and stands at the door of Elisha's house. Elisha sends a messenger out to him, saying go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Naaman is wroth and goes away, saying he thought the prophet would surely come out to him, stand, call on the name of the Lord his God, strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper. He complains in his pride that this was not the process he expected.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: He asks whether Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, are not better than all the waters of Israel, and turns away in a rage, thinking of a physical cleansing rather than a spiritual one. His mind is carnal, not thinking as the prophet thinks.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: His servants come near and reason with him, that if the prophet had bidden him do some great thing he would have done it; how much rather then when he says only wash and be clean. Taking heed, Naaman goes down and dips himself seven times in Jordan according to the saying of the man of God, and his flesh comes again like the flesh of a little child, and he is clean.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Naaman returns to the man of God with all his company and stands before him, saying, behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. He asks Elisha to take a blessing of his servant.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Elisha says, as the Lord liveth before whom I stand, I will receive none, and though Naaman urges him, he refuses. Naaman asks that he be given two mules' burden of earth, for from now on he will offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods but to the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: He asks that the Lord pardon him in one thing, that when his master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship and leans on his hand, and he bows there, the Lord pardon his servant. Elisha says, go in peace, and Naaman departs a little way.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, reasons that his master has spared Naaman the Syrian by not receiving what he brought, and swears, as the Lord liveth, he will run after him and take somewhat of him. When Naaman sees him running, he lights down from the chariot to meet him and asks whether all is well.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Gehazi lies, saying his master has sent him, that two young men of the sons of the prophets have come from mount Ephraim, and asks for a talent of silver and two changes of garments. Naaman urges him to take two talents, binds them in two bags with two changes of garments, and lays them on two of his servants to carry before Gehazi.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: When Gehazi comes to the tower, he takes the goods from their hand, bestows them in the house, and sends the men away, hiding what he took like a thief.
